952:
The city manager shall establish procedures which shall insure that when a utility customer calls the city hall to schedule a utility hearing time, such customer will be promptly notified of the date, time and place of such hearing (to include the room number at the city hall where the hearing will be conducted), and shall further notify such customer of the person designated as hearing officer.
(Code 1977, § 22-36)
953:
The city manager shall designate a hearing officer to conduct the hearings provided for by this article. Such designation may be on a rotating basis, or the designated hearing officer may be changed from time to time, but in every instance the hearing officer shall be a responsible city employee. In no instance may the hearing officer be an elected official of the city.
(Code 1977, § 22-37)
954:
The hearings provided for by this article shall not be conspicuously conducted, i.e., they shall transpire in a relatively private place and not in the presence of customers paying bills or city employees not involved in the determination of the merits of the subject matter of the hearing. However, the hearing officer hereby has the authority to call for and promptly receive all city records and all testimony of any city employees such as would tend to shed any light on the merits of the complaining customers' contentions, the city's billing position, or any other information bearing upon the subject matter of the hearing.
(Code 1977, § 22-38)
955:
At hearings provided for by this article the only relevant issue is whether or not the complaining customer was billed for utilities' services or garbage collection actually received, and according to the city's standard charges therefor. Evidence as to any other matter relating to utility services or garbage collection, or any other complaint against the city, shall not be heard.
(Code 1977, § 22-39)
956:

(Code 1977, § 22-40)
957:

If the complaining customer pays the adjusted charge before the cutoff date there shall be no termination of city services. If the complaining customer does not pay the adjusted charges before the cutoff date city services shall be terminated; however, the adjusted charges shall prevail. If the hearing officer determines that the complaining customer's charges are proper, services shall be terminated on the cutoff date unless the bill or statement is paid in full prior to the cutoff date.
(Code 1977, § 22-41)
958:

959:

(Code 1977, § 22-43)

965:
Unless the context specifically indicates otherwise, the meaning of terms used in this article shall be as follows:
Abnormal strength wastewater means any wastewater with BOD and suspended solids concentrations greater than that of normal strength wastewater but which is otherwise acceptable into a public sewer under the terms of the sewer use ordinance.
Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) means the quantity of oxygen utilized in the biochemical oxidation of organic matter in five (5) days at twenty (20) degrees Celsius by the laboratory procedure prescribed in Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater. BOD shall be expressed in milligrams per liter.
Domestic wastewater discharger means any discharger not covered under the definition of "industrial wastewater discharger."
Industrial wastewater discharger means any nongovernmental industrial or commercial establishment with a classification as designated in the Standard Industrial Classification Manual, latest edition, U.S. Office of Management and Budget and who utilizes the wastewater treatment works of the city.
Infiltration/inflow means water other than wastewater that enters a sewerage system.
Normal strength wastewater means wastewater with BOD and suspended solids concentrations less than or equal to that permitted by the sewer use ordinance and which is otherwise acceptable into a public sewer under the terms of the sewer use ordinance.
Suspended solids means suspended matter that either floats on the surface of, or is in suspension in, water, wastewater or other liquids, and that is removable by laboratory filtering as prescribed in Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater. Suspended solids shall be expressed in milligrams per liter.
Toxic pollutants means any substance whether gaseous, liquid or solid which, when discharged to a public sewer in sufficient concentrations, may in the opinion of the designated city representative, be hazardous to sewer maintenance and personnel, tend to interfere with any wastewater treatment process, or to constitute a hazard to human beings or animals, or to inhibit aquatic life, or to create a hazard to recreation in the receiving waters of the effluent from a wastewater treatment plant.
(Ord. No. 0-80-6, § 1-2, 2-19-80)
